text:
maya liu: Heads-up — since the adaptive-batcher v2 rollout I'm seeing a 95th/99th latency spike for hosted inference. Traces point to host-side parse/streaming overhead (syscalls + small gRPC writes). Wondering if we regressed write coalescing or tokenization hot path. :eyes:

aj patel: Can you paste the profiler/snippets? do we have a perf/flamegraph or strace that shows the write churn?

maya liu: Quick strace summary from one replica (post-rollout):
```
% time     seconds  usecs/call     calls    errors syscall
------ ----------- ----------- --------- --------- --------
49.7     0.250000        1200      208    0      writev
22.3     0.112540         80      140    0      recvfrom
12.1     0.061000         61      100    0      nanosleep
```
Lots of tiny `writev` bursts ~1-2KB each. flamegraph shows host parse loop -> socket::writev dominating CPU.

jin park: Hmm. Two things to check: (1) kernel selector logs — if we're picking a generic kernel for short seqs the runtime can be spending extra CPU on packing/unpacking, and (2) KV cache misses causing extra parse work. Any kernel_selector lines in logs?

maya liu: Found this in runtime logs around requests with small seq_len (6-12):
```
2026-02-18T11:04:33Z kernel_selector.cpp:123 selected kernel=generic_transform impl=cpu_fallback reason="no optimized kernel for seq_len=8 on compute_cap=8.0"
```
So some model shards are falling back to generic paths when seq len small — that increases CPU/alloc churn. Also observed many tiny gRPC frames because the proxy is forwarding tokens immediately instead of coalescing.

dave r.: Two quick experiments: (A) enable write aggregation in host-proxy (ENV HOST_WRITEV_COALESCE=1) which batches in-flight frames for up to 2ms before flush, (B) force the kernel selector to prefer the packed-kernel for short sequences (instrument only) to see delta. Also measure KV cache hit-rate; if many prefixes differ by whitespace we get cache misses.

maya liu: Ran (A) on a canary pool. Results:
```
Before: p95=142ms, p99=312ms, host-cpu=72%
After:  p95=98ms,  p99=168ms, host-cpu=44%
writev syscalls dropped ~64%
```
Significant improvement. No functional regressions observed for ~1k requests. :thumbsup:

aj patel: Nice. What about the kernel selector patch? If using packed path reduces CPU, we can enable heuristics in selector for seq_len<=16. But check correctness/quantization invariants first.

jin park: Also suggest normalizing prefixes pre-tokenize: trim repeated spaces and unify newline sequences. Small diffs in prefix text blow the KV cache. Example quick patch (pseudo):
```
-- input_text = request.prompt
++ input_text = normalize_prefix(request.prompt)
++ def normalize_prefix(s): return re.sub(r"\s+"," ", s.strip())
```
That bumped KV cache hit-rate from ~71% to ~92% in a small replay.

maya liu: I'll open two PRs: one for host-proxy write coalescing (config + tests) and one for prefix normalization in pre-tokenize. For kernel selector I'll open an RFC to gate packed-kernel preference behind an opt-in flag for canary. If packed kernel + coalesce fixes p99 we can flip.

dave r.: Please also add a simple perf test that simulates many concurrent short-seq requests to catch regressions in future. Add a CI job that runs the strace-flame scenario (low QPS but high small-writes).

maya liu: Will do. Created issue and linked PRs in the canary: infra-bot: created issue #789: "grpc writev churn + kernel fallbacks causing host-side latency" and PRs: #450-coalesce-proxy, #451-prefix-normalize.

infra-bot: issue #789 created (assignees: maya liu, dave r., jin park), labels: perf, p0, eng-runtime.

aj patel: Great triage. Next steps: ship coalescing to 20% for 24h, run replay to validate KV hit improvement, then evaluate enabling packed kernel heuristic. Thanks all. :rocket:
